Part of the Exp8 record · Taker imbalance |zNET|, set 1 · wallet inventory shocks in sections 10 and 11

Exp8 unwinders: early and late, fast and slow

How an MM gets out of inventory it absorbed. Section 4.4 splits the 25,705 absorbers that accumulated inventory into early and late unwinders against the price extreme. Sections 10 to 12 read the resting orders of shocked MMs, how fast the population recovers, and how MMs quote while they unwind. Sections 4.4 and 12 are on the taker-imbalance events; sections 10 and 11 are on wallet inventory shocks.

Key results

The SAME-side best quote moves away from the market§10.2 →Revert shocks recover fastest and step shocks hardly at all§11.3 →Inside one MM the lean of record carries no speed§11.5 →In the first 5 minutes after the peak, the measure of record, fast unwinders lean toward the exit and slow unwinders lean away§12.5 →In the first 5 minutes the lean follows the side the MM’s own fills are on, in every speed class§12.5 →The faster the unwind, the more the exit-side taker rate rises right after the peak§12.6 →

Section, table and figure numbers are those of the single Exp8 record, so they do not start at 1 here. Definitions shared by every section are in the notation and event-set sections of the main page.

Each finding shows its headline. Click one to read the explanation.

4.4 Early and late unwinders among absorbers that accumulated inventory

Section 4.4 of the Exp8 record. Its population, the event window and the active rule are defined in §4.1 on the main page.

Symbols used on this page (early and late unwinders)

Symbols used on this page (early and late unwinders)

  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • A and t*: A (accumulation) is the most HYPE the MM built on the absorption side at any minute inside the event window, counted from its position at t0. t* is the end of the first minute at which that maximum is reached: the MM's own inventory peak. Two MMs in one event have different t*.
  • L: the level at the peak: how far the MM's position at t* sits from its median position over the 6 hours before t0, in HYPE, positive toward the absorption side.
  • One scale for both: A and L are both divided by the same number, that MM's own sig24 for that event. They differ only in the starting point: A counts from the position at t0, L from the 6-hour median.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Price extreme text: the minute of the highest mid (up move) or lowest mid (down move) from t0 to 30 minutes after t1.
  • G: the share of A the MM has already given back at text.
  • Early, late: early: t* at or before text and G at least one half. Late, held more than half: t* at or before text and G under one half. Late, peak after the price extreme: t* later than text.
  • PRE2H, ACC, UNW: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; ACC runs from t0 to t*; UNW is the 2 hours after t*.
  • Markout M30, M60: what a fill is worth against the mid 30, 60 or 120 minutes later, in bps of the fill's USD; positive is favourable to the wallet.
  • Unwind length, censored: minutes after t* until 60% of the peak inventory A* is given back; a value at the cap means the MM still held more than 40% of it when the 6-hour search ended.

Timing is measured only on MMs whose inventory actually grew on the absorption side during the event. 25,705 of the 126,846 event × active-MM rows clear that bar, a median 23 per event, and they hold 64% of all hit-side maker USD. Early means half of the accumulation was already gone when the price reached its extreme.

Which MMs the timing split is measured on, how early and late are decided, and what each row of the table measures

Symbols used in this section

  • MM is a market maker: a wallet the MM label model calls a HYPE market maker on that date. An active MM also has at least one fill in the two hours before the event and at least one fill during it, the fill-based gate; the post-only rule of §4.1 is not applied here. One row is one event × active MM.
  • t0 and t1 are the start and end of the event window [t0,t1): 30 minutes for 84% of events, at most 180 minutes. PRE2H is the two hours ending at t0.
  • Absorption side is the maker side that fills the surging takers. s=+1 when takers sell, so absorbing them makes the MM longer, and s=−1 when takers buy.
  • qt is the MM's HYPE position at the end of the 1-minute bin ending at t. xt=s (qt−qt0) is the inventory built since the window start, positive toward the absorption side.
  • A, the accumulation, is the largest xt over the window's minutes: the most inventory the event built, counted from the position at t0. tw, the in-window peak, is the first minute where xt reaches A. A and tw decide which MMs this section measures.
  • t*, the inventory peak, and A*, the peak inventory, follow the MM past the window end. From tw the peak moves with every new high the inventory makes, and the search stops at the first minute the MM has given back 60% of its highest inventory so far, or 60 minutes after t1, whichever comes first. A* is the inventory at t*. An MM that holds 1,000 HYPE at minute 25 of a 30-minute window, keeps buying to 1,400 HYPE by minute 50 and is down to 500 HYPE by minute 70 has tw at minute 25, t* at minute 50 and A* of 1,400 HYPE. Two MMs in one event have different t*.
  • L, the level at the in-window peak, is L=s (qtw−median6h q), with the median over the six hours before t0: how far the peak position sits from the MM's normal position.
  • sig24, the MM's own scale, is sig24=max[1.4826 MAD(q−median6hq), 0.02 p95|q|, 12500/mid] in HYPE, every term over the 24 hours before the event. The first term is the typical distance of the position from its six-hour median, measured robustly. The other two are floors: 2% of the 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE. It is one number per MM per event.
  • Shocked means |dq|≥3 sig24, where dq=qt1−qt0 is the window's end-minus-start position change.

How A and L differ

A and L are compared with the same sig24. They differ only in the starting position. A counts from the position at t0. L counts from the six-hour median. The two disagree when the MM starts the window away from its median. Take an MM with sig24=1,000 HYPE on an event where takers sell (s=+1):

  • It starts 2,000 HYPE short of its median and buys 2,000 HYPE. Then A is 2 sig24 but L is 0: the event only brought it back to normal.
  • It starts 2,000 HYPE long of its median and buys 500 HYPE. Then L is 2.5 sig24 but A is 0.5 sig24: it was already long before the event.

Which MMs are in the population

An absorber that accumulated inventory is an active MM in one event with all three of

  • A≥sig24: the event built at least one sig24 of inventory;
  • L≥sig24: the peak position is at least one sig24 on the absorption side of the six-hour median;
  • the fill condition: absorption-side maker fills larger than all opposite-side fills over [t0,tw), in HYPE, so the inventory came from filling takers and not from the MM's own crossing orders.

The shock rule needs |dq|≥3 sig24 on the end-minus-start change. This rule needs 1 sig24 at the in-window peak. 5,857 of the 25,705 admitted rows are also shocked.

How early and late are decided

The price extreme text is the minute of the highest 1-minute mid over [t0,t1+60 min) when the event's price move is up, and of the lowest when it is down, so it covers the same span as the peak search. The share of the peak inventory already given back at that minute is

G=1−xtextA*

read at the end of the extreme minute. G is a share of A*: 0% still holds all of it, 50% has shed half, 100% is back at the window-start position, above 100% has gone past that level, and a negative value means the MM held more than A*. A row is early when t*≤text and G≥0.5, and late otherwise. Late has two shapes: held more than half when the peak is at or before the extreme and G is under 0.5, and peak after the price extreme when the MM was still building after the price had turned. The extreme falls after the window in 65.7% of events and on the last minute of the 60-minute extension in 2.7%.

The three phases

  • PRE2H is [t0−2 h,t0), the MM's own baseline before the event.
  • ACC, the accumulation phase, is [t0,t*): the window start to the MM's own inventory peak. Its length is the inventory peak minute row of the table below, a median 19 minutes for early rows, 27 for late rows that held more than half and 76 for late rows whose peak came after the extreme.
  • UNW, the unwind phase, is [t*,t*+T60), where T60 is the minutes from the peak to the first minute the MM holds 0.4 A* or less. The phase ends when the MM has given back 60% of what it built, so its length is the length of that MM's unwind: a median 5 minutes for early rows, 56 for held more than half and 314 for peak after the extreme.
  • The 6-hour cap. T60 is searched for 360 minutes after t*. A row that never gets there is censored: its UNW is the full six hours and it is counted in the share censored at 360 min row. That is 0.2% of early rows, 21.2% of held more than half and 47.2% of peak after the extreme.

What each row of the table measures

  • Given back at the price extreme is G; given back at the event end is the same ratio at t1. Both are negative when the MM held more than A* at that minute.
  • Minute rows count from t0. A peak minute above the window length is a peak that fell after t1.
  • Taker share is crossing fill USD over all fill USD, inside the event window [t0,t1) (event) or inside UNW (unwind).
  • Submits / PRE2H is the phase's submits per minute on that side over the same MM's PRE2H rate on that side. Rows with no PRE2H submits on that side are dropped.
  • Maker M30 and M60 are markouts of the phase's maker fills at 30 and 60 minutes, in bps. One fill of size q HYPE at price p with mid m 30 minutes later marks out d (m−p) q dollars, with d=+1 for a buy and −1 for a sell. The row value sums these over the phase's maker fills and divides by the same fills' USD. Positive means the price moved in the MM's favour.
  • Markout rows pool both sides unless the row names a side. Absorption-side fills add to the event's inventory; exit-side fills reduce it. A one-sided markout mostly follows the price path, so read it against the same MM's PRE2H value, which is in the source table.
  • UNW fills / A* is the MM's UNW maker fills on that side in HYPE over its peak inventory.
  • Minutes back to the window-start position uses the same clock as T60 with the level x≤0, and is capped at 360 minutes the same way.
  • UNW best-level distance is the distance from the mid to the nearest resting order on that side, in bps, median over the UNW minutes with an order there, and the skew tables of this section measure the same distance to the same-side touch instead. UNW resting size averages every UNW minute, zero-quote minutes included.

Column key and source
All 914 events, 126,846 event × active-MM rows, 2025-10-10 included. A (accumulation) is the most inventory the event built, counted from the MM's position at the window start t0. L (level at the in-window peak) is the peak position counted from the MM's median position over the six hours before t0. Both are in HYPE and positive toward the absorption side, the maker side that fills the surging takers. Both are compared with the same sig24, the MM's own position scale over the 24 hours before the event (§4.4). Every row also requires the fill condition: absorption-side maker fills larger than all opposite-side fills between t0 and the in-window peak. rows = event × MM rows admitted; per event = median over events of the number admitted; also shocked and not shocked split the admitted rows by |dq|≥3 sig24, with dq the window's end-minus-start position change; hit-side maker USD, pooled = admitted rows' maker USD on the side the takers hit, over all active MMs' maker USD on that side, summed over events; per-event median = the same share computed per event, then the median; start 1 sig24 on the opposite side = share of admitted rows whose position at t0 was already at least one sig24 on the opposite side of the six-hour median. The bold row is the rule used in the rest of this section. Source tables/review0915_unwind_absorber_variants.csv, which also carries the 2025-10-10-excluded sample, 0.5 and 2 sig24 versions of every rule, and the rule without the fill condition.
  • What A, L and sig24 are in the next item: A is the most HYPE the MM built on the absorption side inside the window, counted from its position at the window start t0. L is how far its position at that peak sits from its median position over the 6 hours before t0. Both are divided by one number, sig24: that MM's own typical position swing over the 24 hours before t0, in HYPE, never less than $12,500 of HYPE. Example with sig24 = 1,000 HYPE, takers selling. An MM that starts 2,000 HYPE short of its median and buys 2,000 has A = 2 sig24 and L = 0: the event only brought it back to normal. An MM that starts 2,000 HYPE long and buys 500 has L = 2.5 sig24 and A = 0.5 sig24: it was already long. Each test alone admits one of these two, so the rule asks for both.
  • A≥sig24 and L≥sig24 remove different MMs, so the rule requires both.
    A≥sig24 alone admits 31,406 rows. 19.9% of them started the window at least one sig24 on the opposite side of their six-hour median, so absorbing the takers moved them back toward their normal position. L≥sig24 alone admits 35,330 rows. Some of them were already far from their median before the window and built little inside it: their median A is 1.72 sig24, against 2.33 sig24 under the rule used here.
  • 1 sig24 is the threshold that keeps most of the absorption while keeping the measured quantity meaningful.
    Requiring both at 0.5 sig24 admits 38,114 rows holding 74% of hit-side maker USD. At 1 sig24, 25,705 rows hold 64%. At 2 sig24, 13,312 rows hold 45%. At 0.5 sig24 an MM at the $12,500 floor is admitted with $6,250 of inventory, too small for "gave back half" to mean anything.
  • The rule selects the wallets that carry the event, and the shock rule is not what selects them.
    65% of each event's five biggest absorbers accumulate inventory by this rule, against 23.6% flagged by the shock rule (§8.2). 5,857 of the 25,705 admitted rows are shocked, and 1,635 of the 7,492 shocked wallet-events (fill-based gate, all dates) are outside it: 872 of those ended the window with the position moved against the absorption side, and 536 had A≥sig24 but L< sig24.

Column key and source
  • Cells list p5, p25, p50 (bold), p75 and p95 over wallet-events. Rows with a single number are shares of the column.
  • Sample. The 25,705 absorbers that accumulated inventory, admitted on the in-window rule of the two tables above; they fall on 912 of the 914 net-flow events, 2025-10-10 included. Columns: early (6,067 rows); late (19,638), the union of the last two columns; late, held more than half (12,490); late, peak after the price extreme (7,148).
  • Peak and phases. t* is the MM's own inventory peak, followed past the window while the inventory makes new highs and stopped at the first 60% drawdown, at most 60 minutes after t1; A* is the inventory there. ACC = [t0,t*). UNW = [t*,t*+T60), which ends when 60% of A* is given back and is capped at 6 hours. PRE2H = the two hours before t0.
  • Classes. Early: peak at or before the price extreme and at least 50% given back there. Late, held more than half: peak at or before the extreme, under 50% given back. Late, peak after the price extreme: peak after it. The extreme is the highest (price up) or lowest (price down) 1-minute mid over [t0,t1+60 min).
  • Markouts are USD-weighted markouts of the phase's maker fills at 30 and 60 minutes, in bps (basis points, 0.01%), positive when the price moved in the MM's favour. Rows naming no side pool both sides. A wallet-event with no maker fill on that side has no value on that row, so n differs by row; the source table carries it.
  • Censoring. A row that never gives back 60% of A* within 360 minutes of t* is censored: its UNW is the full six hours, and its T60 and minutes back to the window-start position cells hold the 360-minute cap rather than a measured time.
  • Source tables/review0917_phase_table12.csv, built by code/review0917_phase_build.py, review0917_phase_orders.py and review0917_phase_reduce.py. PRE2H submit rates come from the order-day-fixed population build (§4.1).
  • An early unwind takes 5 minutes, a held-more-than-half unwind 56 minutes, and a peak-after-the-extreme unwind 314 minutes.
    These are medians of the minutes from the peak to 60% given back. 23.5% of rows never get there within six hours: 0.2% of early rows, 21.2% of held more than half and 47.2% of peak after the extreme.
  • 37.2% of the peaks fall after the window ends.
    That is 4.7% of early rows, 28.0% of held more than half and 81.0% of peak after the extreme. 9.8% of the peak-after rows are still making new highs when the search stops 60 minutes after t1.
  • Exit-side fills make money while an early MM is unwinding and lose money for both late classes.
    UNW exit-side M30 is +19.3 bps for early rows, −10.2 for held more than half and −7.5 for peak after the extreme. Early MMs exit while the price is still running their way, and the late classes exit after it has turned: the same markout is +33.4 bps when the peak comes 30 or more minutes before the price extreme and −33.3 bps when it comes within 5 minutes of it.
  • Accumulation costs the absorption side in both early and held-more-than-half rows.
    ACC absorption-side M30 is −63.3 bps for early rows and −34.9 for held more than half, against +4.7 for peak after the extreme, whose peaks sit past the price turn.
  • Neither class crosses the spread to get out.
    The median unwind taker share is zero in every column; the p75 is 12.9% for early rows, 8.9% for held more than half and 50.4% for peak after the extreme.
  • The position leaves through maker fills on the exit side, at about four fifths of the peak inventory for early rows.
    UNW exit-side maker fills are 0.82 times A* for early rows, 0.79 for held more than half and 0.61 for peak after the extreme, against absorption-side fills of 0.06, 0.17 and 0.19 times A* in the same window.
  • During the unwind the exit-side quote sits nearer the touch than the absorption-side quote in every class.
    The median early row rests its nearest exit-side order +5.5 bps from the mid against +12.4 bps on the absorption side, and its exit-side resting size is 489 HYPE against 215 HYPE. For held more than half the distances are +8.0 and +14.0 bps.
  • The exit side also carries the message rate.
    UNW submits are 1.78 times the MM's own PRE2H rate on the exit side for early rows and 1.06 times on the absorption side; for held more than half, 1.35 and 0.89.

Remarks that need attention. Readings of the table that the timing class does not yet account for.

  • The UNW quote and size rows compare windows of different lengths.
    UNW runs a median 5 minutes for early rows and 314 for peak-after rows, so an exit-side distance of +5.5 bps against +6.8 bps mixes the lean with the length of the window it is averaged over. Needs attention: settled by comparing the two classes at equal shares of the position still held.
  • The censored rows carry a UNW of exactly six hours.
    47.2% of peak-after rows and 21.2% of held-more-than-half rows never give back 60%, so their markout, quote and size cells average a six-hour window whose end is set by the cap. Needs attention: settled by repeating the class medians on the rows that reach 60% inside the cap.
Where the markout sign comes from, which rows are censored, and what the peak search limit and the old two-hour window change

Symbols used in these tables

  • t0 and t1 are the start and end of the event window. x is the inventory built since t0, positive toward the absorption side. tw is the in-window peak, t* the MM's own peak and A* the inventory there.
  • ACC = [t0,t*); UNW = [t*,t*+T60), ending when 60% of A* is given back, capped at 6 hours. Maker M30 is the USD-weighted 30-minute markout of the phase's maker fills, in bps, positive when the price moved in the MM's favour.
  • Hit-side taker flow is taker USD per minute on the side the event's takers hit. Censored means the MM never gave back 60% of A* within 360 minutes of t*.

Order skew by timing class

Over the minutes an MM is unwinding, its exit-side quote sits nearer the touch than its absorption-side quote in every class. In the 5 minutes after the peak the early class moves its best-quote skew 4.11 bps toward the exit against its own pre-event value, the late, held more than half class 3.29 bps and the late, peak after the price extreme class 1.00 bps. Over the unwind window itself the three changes are −5.44, −3.02 and −1.88 bps.

Symbols used here

  • Population. The 25,705 absorbers that accumulated inventory (event × MM rows, all 914 events, 2025-10-10 included), in the three classes of this section: early (6,067 rows), late, held more than half (12,490) and late, peak after the price extreme (7,148). The text shortens the two late names to late held and late peak-after.
  • t0 is the clock time at which the event window starts. t* is the MM’s own inventory peak, which may fall up to 60 minutes after the window ends, and A* is the inventory there. T60 is the minutes from t* until the MM has given back 60% of A*.
  • Absorption side is the side of the MM’s quotes that fills the surging takers: the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy. Exit side is the other side, whose fills reduce the inventory the event built.
  • Touch is the best price of the whole book on the same side as the order, read as the last book state before the minute. The distance of a bid at price p is 104 (best bid − p) / mid bps, and of an ask 104 (p − best ask) / mid bps. Zero means at the touch.
  • Three measures, one sign: exit minus absorption.
    Δbest = Dbest(exit) − Dbest(absorption)    Δvw = Dvw(exit) − Dvw(absorption)    Δsize = Q(exit) − Q(absorption)Dbest is the distance of the MM’s nearest resting order on that side to the touch, Dvw the size-weighted mean distance of all its resting orders on that side, and Q its resting size on that side in HYPE. A negative Δbest or Δvw means the exit side sits nearer the touch; a positive Δsize means more size rests on the exit side. The exit share of resting size, Q(exit) / [Q(exit) + Q(absorption)], is the same comparison without the MM’s scale; 0.5 is a balanced book.
  • Window values. Orders are read on 1-minute snapshots. Over a window, Dbest is the median over the minutes with an order on that side, Dvw is weighted over all order-minutes, and Q is the mean per minute with empty minutes counted as zero.
  • Windows, in clock order. PRE2H = [t0 − 2 h, t0); ACC = [t0, t*); M5 = [t*, t* + 5 min); M15 = [t*, t* + 15 min); UNW = [t*, t* + T60), capped at 6 hours. M5 lies inside M15, and both lie inside UNW for rows whose unwind runs longer than they do. UNW is a median 5 minutes for early rows, 56 for late held and 314 for late peak-after.
  • Change from PRE2H is a window’s value minus the same MM’s value in PRE2H of the same event. It removes the differences in book scale between classes.

Book size differs by class: the median early row rests 381.0 HYPE on the exit side before the event, the median late held row 199.1 and the median late peak-after row 29.1. The tables below therefore state each window as a change from the same MM’s PRE2H value, and the findings quote those changes.

  • The sooner a class unwinds, the harder it leans toward the exit in the 5 minutes after the peak: 4.11 bps for early rows, 3.29 for late held and 1.00 for late peak-after.
    These are medians of M5 minus the same MM’s PRE2H value, on 4,111, 7,562 and 3,774 rows. 79.4% of early rows move toward the exit, against 71.1% and 57.8%. The size-weighted distance moves the same way by −2.35, −1.89 and −1.37 bps.
  • While they accumulate, the late classes hold their exit-side quote farther from the touch than their absorption-side quote: +0.48 bps for late held and +2.20 bps for late peak-after, against −0.50 bps for early.
    As changes from PRE2H the three are +0.21, +1.02 and −0.42 bps. A distance grows both when the touch moves away from a resting order and when the MM moves the order, and the measure combines the two.
  • The same order holds in size: a class that unwinds sooner moves more of its resting HYPE to the exit side while it does, +40.7 HYPE for early rows against +23.0 for late held and +0.3 for late peak-after.
    The exit share of resting size in M5 is 0.554, 0.539 and 0.500 at the median, from 0.500, 0.498 and 0.491 in PRE2H; over UNW it is 0.586, 0.529 and 0.503.

Remarks that need attention. Readings of the same tables that the timing class does not yet account for.

  • The lean lasts as long as the unwind does, and it is largest for the class that unwinds fastest: −5.44 bps for early rows, −3.02 for late held and −1.88 for late peak-after.
    Needs attention: UNW is a median 5 minutes for early rows, 56 for late held and 314 for late peak-after, so the three numbers average windows of different lengths. Settled by comparing the classes at equal shares of the position still held.
  • The side that moves after the peak is the absorption side, not the exit side.
    From PRE2H to M5 the median early row’s absorption-side best quote moves +2.67 bps and its exit-side best quote −0.54 bps. For late held rows the two are +2.29 and −0.21 bps, and for late peak-after rows +0.54 and 0.00 bps. Needs attention: a 1-minute snapshot cannot separate an order the MM cancelled from one a fill consumed, so the absorption-side move mixes the two. Settled by the cancel and submit counts of the order stream.

Limits

  • The measures are descriptive. The touch moves during the event, so a distance can change while the MM’s order stays at the same price.
  • Figure 9 and Figure 10 cover the shocked rows only, 5,857 of 25,705: 668 early, 3,205 late held and 1,984 late peak-after wallet-events. On the window measures the median M5 change of the best-quote difference is −5.10, −3.63 and −1.24 bps on the shocked rows, against −4.11, −3.29 and −1.00 bps on all rows.
  • A distance difference needs a resting order on both sides. In M5 that holds for 68.3% of early, 61.2% of late held and 54.2% of late peak-after rows; rows quoting one side only enter the size panels alone.
  • UNW runs a median 5 minutes for early rows and 314 for late peak-after rows, so its class medians compare windows of different lengths. M5 and M15 are the same length in every class.
  • The stored 1-minute quotes end 2 hours after the in-window peak, so Figure 9 loses rows after the peak for the classes whose peak moved later: the median wallet-event has 118 (early), 118 (late held) and 84 (late peak-after) stored minutes after t*.
  • Quotes are read at the minute instant. 23.4% of early, 24.2% of late held and 41.5% of late peak-after wallet-minutes have nothing resting at that instant and enter no minute-grain size measure.

10. Resting orders after a roster shock

Event set 4: all 181 roster wallet shocks. Windows are anchored on form_start and the peak bin, read as 5-minute bin labels, which puts every window five minutes early (§15).
Symbols used in sections 10 and 11 (resting orders and recovery)

Symbols used in sections 10 and 11 (resting orders and recovery)

  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Roster shock: a roster MM's inventory deviates by at least 6 of its own trailing 7-day scale and at least $100k.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Bin labels: wallet-shock times are 5-minute bin labels of an end-of-bin position; clock time is the label plus 5 minutes.
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the side whose fills built the wallet's position (bids for a long shock); OPP is the side whose fills reduce it.
  • Quote distance: how far the MM's own best quote on a side sits behind the market's best price on that side, in bps of the mid; 0 means at the touch.
  • Quote gap: accumulating-side quote distance minus unwind-side quote distance, in bps; positive means the exit quote is nearer the market.
  • Reaction latency: time from the taker-surge onset until the MM either drops its resting hit-side size to half its value at onset or moves its best hit-side quote 10 bps further out, on a 1-minute grid.
  • Population shock: the roster-shock detector run unchanged on all 148 population MMs (812 shocks on 88 MMs).
  • T50, T60, T75: minutes after the shock's peak until 50%, 60% or 75% of the peak excursion is given back, on the 5-minute exchange-reported position, capped at 360 minutes (360 = not reached within 6 hours).
  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours). It is measured from the event end t1 on the position change over the event, so it is not the §4.4 unwind length T60, which runs from the MM’s own peak until 60% of the peak inventory is given back.
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale over the 24 hours before t0, in HYPE, never below $12,500 of HYPE.
  • Shocked: the MM's position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 of its own sig24.

After the inventory peak the shocked MM moves its accumulating-side best quote away from the market and leaves its unwind-side quote almost where it was. Resting size stays close to balanced. Both sides are cancelled and reposted faster. The quote gap between the two sides is mostly gone within two hours.

Population and grain
  • Population. All 181 shocks of Exp8's frozen roster catalogue, on 9 of the roster ten: MM01 53, MM02 46, MM05 25, MM03 18, MM07 16, MM04 9, MM09 8, MM10 4, MM08 2. 125 up and 56 down; 125 revert, 32 step, 24 partial; 60 ALONE, 64 FEW, 56 BROAD, 1 unclassified. Only the shocked wallet is read. Exp9 names wallets by roster rank, and rank rk is MM0k here.
  • Grain. The wallet's resting orders rebuilt from the raw HYPE order stream and valued at every minute-end from 24 hours before the build to 6 hours after the peak. 930,121,285 order events (posts, cancels, fills) are stored. A resting order is an ALO or GTC limit order the exchange accepted; rejected orders never rested and are excluded.
  • Clock. Windows are anchored on the catalogue's 5-minute bin labels, the convention the data notes flag as five minutes early.

10.1 Definitions

Sides, windows and measures
  • SAME and OPP. SAME is the side whose fills built the position: the bid after an up shock, the ask after a down shock. OPP is the other side, the one whose fills unwind it. Every paired measure is signed so that a positive value leans toward getting out, which lets up and down shocks pool.
  • Distance to the market's best. For a resting order at price p, with mid m and the market's best price b on the same side (last book state at or before the minute-end), dbid=104×b−pm,  dask=104×p−bm. 0 is at the market's best, positive is behind it, negative improves on it. dSAME and dOPP are the distances of the wallet's own best quote on each side. The distance from mid uses m in place of b.
  • Quote gap. A=dSAME−dOPP in bps, per minute. Positive means the side that built the position is quoted further from the market.
  • Depth skew. With Q the resting notional in USD on a side, K=QOPP−QSAMEQOPP+QSAME.
  • Distance buckets. Touch: d≤0. Near: 0<d≤10 bps. Mid: 10<d≤100 bps. Far: d>100 bps. HYPE's tick is $0.001, which is 0.25 bps at $40.
  • Post and cancel imbalance in bucket b. With Pb the USD posted in the bucket in the minute, ΠPb = PbOPP−PbSAMEPbOPP+PbSAME. ΠCb is the same on cancelled USD. Both are undefined in a minute with no flow in the bucket.
  • Withdrawal rate and fill-through. w=Ct/Qt−1, cancelled USD in the minute over resting USD at the previous minute-end, per side. φSAME is the same ratio on maker-filled USD. Order lifetime at cancel is the median age of the orders cancelled in the minute.
  • Windows. PRE = [form_start − 2 h, form_start), the reference. FORM = [form_start, peak]. PEAK = peak ± 2 min. POST1 = (peak, peak + 30 min]. POST2 = (peak + 30 min, peak + 2 h]. TAIL = (peak + 2 h, peak + 6 h]. BASE = [form_start − 24 h, form_start − 2 h), active minutes only.
  • Statistic. Per shock, the median of a 1-minute measure over the window's minutes. Tables show the median of those per-shock values across shocks. A change is the per-shock paired difference against the same shock's PRE, and its share is the share of shocks with the predicted sign (a prediction of ≥ 0 counts zeros).
  • Reaction latency (seconds). From the taker-surge onset, the first minute in [form_start − 15 min, peak] with hit-side taker USD at least 3 times its BASE median, to the first minute with QSAME≤0.5 times its onset value or dSAME at least 10 bps wider than at onset. Refill: the first minute after the peak with QSAME at 80% or more of its BASE median.

10.2 Quote distance and size by window

Terms used here: SAME, OPP, Roster shock, form_start, peak, Touch, Quote gap, Quantile cells
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the side whose fills built the wallet's position (bids for a long shock); OPP is the side whose fills reduce it.
  • Roster shock: one roster MM's inventory deviates from its trailing level by at least 6 of its own trailing 7-day scale, with a peak deviation of at least $100k (181 shocks). This is a different rule from the 3 sig24 rule of §4.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Touch: the market's best price on that side: the best bid for a bid, the best ask for an ask.
  • Quote gap: accumulating-side quote distance minus unwind-side quote distance, in bps; positive means the exit quote is nearer the market.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.

Column key and source
One row per measure. SAME and OPP rows are the two sides of the same wallet; pair rows combine them. Window cells are the cross-shock median of the per-shock window median, with p25 / p75 below; the source table carries no p5 or p95. Change cells are the median paired change against PRE, with the share of shocks whose change has the predicted sign and the number of shocks with both windows defined. Predicted sign is the sign set in advance for an MM that reshapes its book to get out. Imbalances are coarse: they are ±1 in any minute where only one side acted. Source Exp9/tables/pre_vs_post_windows.csv, which also holds PEAK, BASE, the FORM change, Wilcoxon p-values and ten further measures (refresh rates, fill-through, presence, mid and far buckets).
  • The SAME-side best quote moves away from the market.
    It sits 3.25 bps behind the market's best in PRE, the two hours before form_start, and 5.88 bps in POST1, the half hour after the peak: a paired +1.36 bps, in 81% of 179 shocks. The change is +0.31 bps by the next hour and a half, POST2.
  • The OPP-side best quote moves less than a tick.
    The paired change is −0.19 bps in POST1, in the predicted direction for 60% of 181 shocks (Wilcoxon p = 0.016).
  • The quote gap widens by 2.07 bps and mostly reverses.
    It rises in 80% of 176 shocks in POST1 and is +0.50 bps above PRE in POST2.
  • The OPP quote almost never reaches the market's best.
    The share of minutes with the OPP quote at or better than the market's best is 0.000 in every window for 178 of 181 shocks.
  • Resting size barely shifts at the median, but a quarter of shocks shift it a lot.
    Depth skew K, OPP minus SAME resting USD over their sum, rises by a median 0.007 (76% of 181 positive); in POST1 its p75 is 0.42. SAME resting notional falls by a median 5.5 kUSD (70% of 181) and is back within 0.03 kUSD of PRE by POST2.
  • Both sides are cancelled and reposted faster, and both keep an order resting in every minute.
    The SAME withdrawal rate, cancelled USD per minute over resting USD, rises from 5.80 to 7.99 (+1.32, 68% of 177) and the OPP rate from 5.77 to 6.88 (+0.81). Presence, the share of minutes with a resting order, is 1.00 on both sides in every window. The median age of cancelled orders is 1.0 to 1.5 seconds in every window.
  • SAME fills concentrate at the peak.
    SAME fill-through, maker-filled USD per minute over resting USD, is 0.044 in PEAK, the minutes around the peak, 0.010 in FORM and at most 0.001 in every other window.
  • New posting moves to the unwind side just behind the best.
    The near-bucket post imbalance, OPP minus SAME USD posted just behind the best over their sum, rises from 0.00 to 0.28, a paired +0.23 in 91% of 181 shocks.

10.4 Reaction latency and refill

Terms used here: SAME, OPP, Roster, form_start, peak, Reaction latency, Censored, Quantile cells
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the side whose fills built the wallet's position (bids for a long shock); OPP is the side whose fills reduce it.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Reaction latency: time from the taker-surge onset until the MM either drops its resting hit-side size to half its value at onset or moves its best hit-side quote 10 bps further out, on a 1-minute grid.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.
  • Taker flow against the MM picks up a median 13 minutes before form_start.
    The onset is the first minute in which taker USD hitting the SAME side is at least 3 times its median from a day before form_start to two hours before it (BASE); it is found in 175 of 181 shocks.
  • The median MM reacts 9 minutes after onset, and 5% take over an hour.
    Latency p25 is 3 minutes and p75 23 minutes; p5 is 1 minute and p95 61 minutes. It is measured on the 165 of 181 shocks with SAME resting size at onset (at form_start for the 6 shocks with no onset), and every one reacts within 6 hours. Halving SAME resting size comes first in 110 shocks and moving the SAME quote 10 bps out in 55.
  • Up and down shocks react at similar speed.
    Median 8 minutes for 117 up shocks and 11.5 minutes for 48 down shocks, p25 3 minutes for both.
  • SAME depth comes back.
    It is at 80% or more of its BASE median by +30 minutes in 152 of the 174 shocks with SAME depth in BASE (87%), by +2 hours in 94% and by +6 hours in 95% of them.
  • Latency does not scale with shock size.
    Within each MM the slope of log latency on log peak deviation is negative for some MMs and positive for others (−1.93 to +0.48).

10.5 The response on a 5-minute grid

Terms used here: SAME, OPP, Roster shock, form_start, peak, Touch, Quote distance, Quote gap
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the side whose fills built the wallet's position (bids for a long shock); OPP is the side whose fills reduce it.
  • Roster shock: one roster MM's inventory deviates from its trailing level by at least 6 of its own trailing 7-day scale, with a peak deviation of at least $100k (181 shocks). This is a different rule from the 3 sig24 rule of §4.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Touch: the market's best price on that side: the best bid for a bid, the best ask for an ask.
  • Quote distance: how far the MM's own best quote on a side sits behind the market's best price on that side, in bps of the mid; 0 means at the touch.
  • Quote gap: accumulating-side quote distance minus unwind-side quote distance, in bps; positive means the exit quote is nearer the market.
  • The SAME best quote starts moving during the build.
    It is 3.4 bps behind the market's best two hours before the peak and already 5.1 bps in the bin before the peak. It is furthest out at 7.8 bps five minutes after the peak and back at 3.8 bps two hours after it.
  • The OPP best quote moves in by less than a bp.
    It is 3.3 bps behind the best before the peak, 2.5 bps at +15 minutes and 3.5 bps at +2 h.
  • SAME resting notional dips; OPP does not move.
    SAME is 0.80 of its BASE median, its median over the day before the build, in the peak bin, 0.68 at +5 minutes and 0.95 at +30. OPP stays at 1.00.
  • Fills move from SAME to OPP within five minutes of the peak.
    Median SAME maker fills are 196 kUSD in the peak bin against 20 to 50 before and 30 at +5 minutes. OPP maker fills peak at 86 kUSD at +5 minutes.
  • Posting rises on OPP only.
    In the peak bin the MM posts 1.63 times its BASE rate of USD on OPP and 1.23 times on SAME. Afterwards only OPP stays above its BASE rate (1.53 at +5 minutes, 1.25 at +30).
  • The paired measures peak in the bin after the peak.
    The quote gap is 4.2 bps at +5 minutes and 0.6 at +60. Depth skew K is 0.22 at +5 and 0.00 by +30. The touch post imbalance is 0.87 at +5, 0.51 at +30 and 0.34 at +60.

Two example shocks

10.6 Limits

What this does not establish
  • 181 shocks on 9 wallets, 99 of them on MM01 and MM02. Many share a date and a market move, so shares describe this set and Wilcoxon p-values overstate certainty.
  • Distances use a book state 0.27 s stale at the median and up to 16 s at p99 on the worst date, so orders near the 0 and 10 bps bucket edges can switch buckets.
  • The −0.19 bps OPP change is one tick or less at HYPE's prices. It is not an improvement of the unwind-side quote.
  • The cancel imbalance does not measure withdrawal for MMs that cancel within seconds; the per-side withdrawal rate is the substitute.
  • Peer MMs in each window (median 7) are stored but not read. Unwind speed and markouts are not measured here.
  • Only the notional-weighted share within 10 bps of the touch describes the shape of the resting orders; the size-weighted mean distance and the distance to the best filled price were not built.
  • Exp10's rebuild of 2025-08-11 found an order-feed gap. Exp9's three shocks of episode 39 (MM01, MM02, MM04) carry 438 orders with no terminal row that the build kept resting; they have not been re-read.

11. Population shocks and recovery speed

Event set 5: 812 population wallet shocks on 88 of 148 MMs. Recovery times run from the peak bin, on clock time. The skew tests read resting orders inside the set-1 boxes: 468 shocks whose peak falls near an event or control window, and 7,492 shocked wallet-events on 642 wallets, of which 2,466 rows are on 63 of the 148.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the maker side the event's takers trade against; the exit side is the other one.
  • Control window: the same clock time and length on the nearest date with no event nearby.
Terms used here: Shocked, Absorption side, exit side, Control window, Population shock, form_start, peak
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.
  • Population shock: the roster-shock detector run unchanged on all 148 population MMs (812 shocks on 88 MMs).
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.

The roster-shock detector finds 812 shocks on 88 of the 148 population MMs. The median shock has given back 60% of its inventory deviation 30 minutes after the peak. On shocked MMs inside net-flow events, MMs that place more of their orders on the exit side get half the position back sooner. For one MM from event to event, that share predicts almost nothing.

Population and grain
  • Population. The 148 wallets with at least 10 active HYPE days, 2025-03-27 to 2026-06-30. Roster wallets are MM01 to MM10; the others are coded P###.
  • Grain. Each wallet's exchange-reported end-of-bin HYPE position on a contiguous 5-minute grid over its active days (4.48 million bins). Inactive days are missing, so no window crosses them. Fills and order submits per bin and side come from hype_mm_5m and hype_mm_5m_orders_ext.
  • Clock. form_start and peak are 5-minute bin labels; the clock time is the label plus 5 minutes, and the skew matching below uses clock time.
  • Quote data. The skew tests read the resting-order state of the population event study (the 915 market taker-imbalance events of the population section), because resting orders are built per event window.

11.1 Definitions

Detector, recovery times, skew measures, samples
  • Detector. Exp8's frozen v2 detector run unchanged: a candidate run of bins with |z| ≥ 6 on an active day, a start observed within 3 h, peak deviation times mid of at least $100k, 60% of the build inside one 25-minute span, a directed build, prominence of at least 1.5 over the 3 h before (and after, except for steps), and Exp8's activity gate. The trailing scale is Exp8's rule rebuilt on this grid: scale=max(1.4826×MAD7d, 0.02×p9530d|q|, 12500/mid) with the MAD taken around the trailing 6-hour median over the wallet's active bins in the trailing 7 days.
  • Actively market making. Gate 1: at least one fill in each of the two hours before form_start. Gate 2: at least one bid submit and one ask submit in those two hours.
  • Excursion and recovery times. With m the median position over the 24 bins before form_start and s=±1 the shock direction, e(t)=s×(q(t)−m) and E is e at the peak. T50, T60, T75 and T100 are the minutes after the peak until e(t)≤0.5E, 0.4E, 0.25E and 0; censored at 360 minutes.
  • Recovery classes. Fast: T60≤30 min. Medium: 30<T60≤120. Slow or held: T60>120 or censored. The cuts align with Exp9's POST1 window and the 2-hour unwind window of the skew measures.
  • Skew measures, per shocked wallet-event and window, signed to the wallet's own exit side. Exit-side submit share: share of order submits on the side that reduces the position (0.5 is balanced). Size skew: resting HYPE on the exit side minus the accumulating side. Best-quote distance skew: exit-side best quote distance from mid minus the accumulating side's, positive when the exit quote is further away. Windows: PRE2H (2 h before the event), ACC (event start to the wallet's own peak) and UNW (own peak to +2 h).
  • Minutes to half (min_to_half). Minutes after the event end until half the wallet's excursion is back, on a 1-minute grid, censored at 360. It is measured from the event end t1 on the position change over the event, so it is not the §4.4 unwind length T60, which runs from the MM’s own peak until 60% of the peak inventory is given back.
  • Samples. Sample (a): the 468 of the 812 shocks whose peak falls inside or within 30 minutes of an event or control window; 298 of them have a wallet-event row. Sample (b): every shocked wallet-event (|zdq| ≥ 3) in an event window, 7,492 rows on 642 wallets (fill-based gate, all dates). Within demeans both variables inside wallets with at least 10 rows; across MMs correlates wallet medians over those 181 wallets.

11.2 Shock counts and frequency

  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet.
Terms used here: Shocked, Roster, Population shock, Wallet codes
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Population shock: the roster-shock detector run unchanged on all 148 population MMs (812 shocks on 88 MMs).
  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet. Codes are local to a section: the same code can name another wallet elsewhere.
  • Prominence is the largest single cut.
    5,586 candidates; 5,183 anchored; 4,304 above $100k; 3,280 sudden; 3,026 directed; 1,240 prominent (1,786 removed, most inside a longer swing); 887 active; 812 after merging overlapping windows.
  • Requiring active market making removes one shock, and every table keeps all 812.
    A fill in each of the two hours before form_start removes none; a bid and an ask order in those hours removes one wallet quoting one side only, leaving 811.
  • The roster shocks a little more often than the rest.
    The roster ten have 200 shocks (166 of the 181 Exp8 catalogue shocks re-detected on the exchange-reported position, plus 34 the catalogue lacks) on 3,198 active days (6.3 per 100); the other 138 wallets have 612 on 12,367 days (4.9 per 100).
  • Shocks concentrate on a minority of wallets.
    60 of the 148 wallets have no shock, 36 have one or two shocks, 31 have three to nine and 21 have ten or more, from 4.9 (P077) to 55.6 (P005; P### codes are non-roster MMs) per 100 active days. MM02 is at 17.0 and MM01 at 11.6.
  • Direction and class. 472 up and 340 down; 536 revert, 184 step and 92 partial.
  • A speed rule finds a superset.
    Replacing the rule that 60% of the build is sudden by a build of at least 3 trailing-scale units in 30 minutes gives 1,151 shocks, including all 812. The extra 339 are large slow builds.

11.3 Recovery times

Terms used here: Event window, Shocked, Roster, Population shock, form_start, peak, Wallet codes, T50, T60, T75, Minutes to half, Censored, rho
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Population shock: the roster-shock detector run unchanged on all 148 population MMs (812 shocks on 88 MMs).
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet. Codes are local to a section: the same code can name another wallet elsewhere.
  • T50, T60, T75: minutes after the shock's peak until 50%, 60% or 75% of the peak excursion is given back, on the 5-minute exchange-reported position, capped at 360 minutes (360 = not reached within 6 hours).
  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours). It is measured from the event end t1 on the position change over the event, so it is not the §4.4 unwind length T60, which runs from the MM’s own peak until 60% of the peak inventory is given back.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • rho: Spearman rank correlation, from −1 to +1; p tests rho = 0.

The fifth row uses the position at form_start as the baseline instead of the pre-2h median. The last row measures the 181 Exp8 roster catalogue shocks the same way on this position series. Source Exp9/tables/pop_recovery.csv; per wallet in pop_recovery_by_wallet.csv.
  • Classes. Fast (back within half an hour) 438 (53.9%), medium (within two hours) 181 (22.3%), slow or held (later or never) 193 (23.8%). With the position at form_start as the baseline, 92.2% of shocks keep their class.
  • Revert shocks recover fastest and step shocks hardly at all.
    Median T60 is 15 minutes for revert shocks, 75 for partial and 360 for step shocks, 51% of which never get 60% back.
  • The roster and the rest recover at similar speed.
    Median T60 is 25 minutes for roster shocks and 30 for the others (p75 96 and 130).
  • Wallets differ widely. Among the 21 wallets with at least 10 shocks, median T60 runs from 5 minutes (P075, all 21 shocks fast) to 360 (P002, 73% slow or held). MM02 is at 15 minutes with 85% fast; MM01 at 105 minutes with 9% fast.
  • Shock frequency does not order recovery speed.
    Spearman ρ between shocks per 100 active days and median T60 is −0.04 (p = 0.75) over the 52 wallets with at least 3 shocks. The profile section reads a related relation on event windows (share of windows shocked against median minutes to half, ρ = −0.24 over 223 wallets); the two use different shock definitions and wallet sets.

11.4 Quote skew and recovery speed

  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • ACC, UNW: ACC (accumulation) runs from t0 to the MM's own inventory peak; UNW (unwind) is the 2 hours after that peak.
Terms used here: sig24, Shocked, Absorption side, exit side, PRE2H, PRE30, POST, ACC, UNW, Submits, cancels, Population shock, Minutes to half, Censored, rho
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • ACC, UNW: ACC (accumulation) runs from t0 to the MM's own inventory peak; UNW (unwind) is the 2 hours after that peak. Each MM has its own boundaries.
  • Submits, cancels: new limit orders and cancels. The venue records a modify as one cancel plus one new order, so cancels per submit sits near 1.
  • Population shock: the roster-shock detector run unchanged on all 148 population MMs (812 shocks on 88 MMs).
  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours). It is measured from the event end t1 on the position change over the event, so it is not the §4.4 unwind length T60, which runs from the MM’s own peak until 60% of the peak inventory is given back.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • rho: Spearman rank correlation, from −1 to +1; p tests rho = 0.

Column key and source
Sample (b), 7,492 shocked wallet-events on 642 wallets; n varies because a distance needs a quote on both sides. A negative ρ means more lean toward the exit goes with faster recovery; for the distance skew the same reading is a positive ρ. Pooled: over wallet-events. Within: both variables demeaned inside wallets with at least 10 rows. Per wallet: median of the per-wallet ρ, with the share of wallets whose ρ is negative. Across MMs: ρ of wallet medians over the 181 wallets. Terciles: median minutes to half in the low, middle and high third of the measure, over wallet-events. Bold marks |ρ| of at least 0.34. Source Exp9/tables/pop_skew_vs_recovery.csv, pop_skew_vs_recovery_cross_wallet.csv, pop_skew_vs_recovery_by_wallet.csv; sample (a) in pop_skew_vs_recovery_sample_a.csv.
  • The relation holds across MMs.
    A wallet's median exit-side submit share during the build ranks its median recovery time with ρ = −0.48 over 181 wallets, and in the unwind window with −0.49. Split the 181 wallets into thirds by that share (wallet terciles; Table 69 splits wallet-events). The lowest third place almost none of their orders on the exit side: their median minutes to half is 360 (share 0.001, 67% censored). It is 174 for the middle third and 95 for the top third (share 0.50, 23% censored).
  • Inside an MM the skew explains little.
    Comparing each MM's events with that MM's own average, the build-window submit share keeps ρ = −0.09 (n = 4,594) and the size skews are at zero.
  • Most of the pooled −0.34 comes from wallet-events that quote one side only.
    1,179 wallet-events (21.7%) post under 10% of their submits on the exit side during the build; their median minutes to half is 360, with 67.5% censored. The 3,677 rows with a share of 0.3 or more have a median of 74 minutes, and among them ρ = −0.07.
  • The correlation is the same for small and large shocks.
    In terciles of the peak excursion in own scale units (medians 3.5, 4.8 and 8.2), the build-window submit-share ρ is −0.31, −0.33 and −0.37.
  • MMs that quote wider recover slower.
    The exit-side best quote's distance from mid has pooled ρ = +0.25 (n = 5,096), and the build-window distance skew has ρ = +0.38 across MMs.
  • Detector shocks near an event add nothing.
    With 136 to 298 of them (sample (a)) on 18 to 24 wallets, every pooled ρ is inside ±0.20 except the build-window distance skew (+0.19, n = 136, p = 0.03).
Limits
  • 344 of the 812 population shocks (217 dates, 64 wallets) fall outside every event and control window and have no quote data, so the skew results rest on shocks inside market events.
  • The across-MM relation is descriptive. Book size, quoting width and one- or two-sided presence differ between wallets at the same time, and the exit-side submit share is correlated with all three.
  • Minutes to half runs from the event end and T60 from the wallet's own peak; the unwind skew window and the recovery clock overlap in time. A fast unwind shortens the part of the window with a reason to skew, which would push the sign positive; the observed sign is negative.
  • The detector re-detects 166 of the 181 Exp8 catalogue shocks on the same wallet in the same peak hour (167 within ±1 h) and finds 34 roster shocks outside the catalogue. The 14 unreproduced and 34 extra roster shocks come from the position series (exchange-reported against Exp8's fill-anchored panel), so population counts that mix the two series disagree at the 5 to 10% level.
  • Controls are left out of the skew tests because their exit side is arbitrary; re-signing them by the wallet's own position change gives the same signs. The speed-rule catalogue is not carried through recovery or skew.

11.5 All 812 shocks: inside one MM, more exit lean does not bring a faster recovery

Resting quotes are now built for all 812 population shocks, including the 344 outside every event window. In the first 5 minutes after its own peak the typical shocked MM moves its exit quote 4.5 bps nearer the touch than its absorption quote, and 81% of shocks lean that way. Inside one MM, the shocks with more lean do not recover faster: within-MM Spearman ρ = −0.03 over 432 shocks on 16 MMs, and on 3 of 16 MMs the fast shocks lean more than the slow ones. The size-share lean orders recovery across MMs (ρ = −0.50 over 19 MMs) and not within one (+0.04), the pattern §11.4 found on market-event rows.

Symbols used in this section
  • MM: one of the 148 population wallets (at least 10 active HYPE days); 88 of them have a shock.
  • Shock: one of the 812 population shocks of §11.2 (Exp8’s frozen v2 detector on the 5-minute exchange-reported position); s = +1 when the position rose, −1 when it fell.
  • t0: build start, the form_start bin label plus 5 minutes (clock time). tp: the peak bin label plus 5 minutes.
  • Own peak t*: the clock minute in [t0, tp + 5 min] where s × (q(t) − q(t0)) is largest, with q the MM’s HYPE position rebuilt from its own fills on a 1-minute grid. Median 1 minute before tp (p5 4 minutes before, p95 2 after).
  • T60: minutes after the peak bin until 60% of the excursion from the median position of the 2 hours before the build is back, 5-minute grid, censored at 360 (§11.3).
  • Classes: fast T60 ≤ 10, medium 10 < T60 ≤ 60, slow T60 > 60 or censored (cuts of record, adopted 2026-09-17); 30 / 120 is the older pair.
  • Exit side: the side whose fills reduce the shock (the ask after a rise). Absorption side: the side that built it.
  • Touch: the market’s best same-side price at the minute instant (ts_bookdiff_lt, backward as-of); distances in bps of the ts_bbo mid, 0 at the touch, positive behind it.
  • Windows: PRE2H [t0 − 2 h, t0); ACC [t0, t*); M5 [t*, t* + 5 min); HELD [t*, t* + min(T60, 120) min); UNW [t*, t* + 2 h).
  • Two-sided quoter: both sides have a resting order in at least half the PRE2H minutes and half the UNW minutes (560 shocks on 56 MMs).
  • Spearman ρ: rank correlation. Across MMs: ρ of MM medians. Within MM: ρ after subtracting each MM’s own mean from both variables.

The lean measures

  • Best-quote skew in window W: skewW = dexit,W − dabs,W, with dside,W the median over the window’s minutes of that side’s best resting quote’s distance to the touch. Negative = the exit quote sits nearer the touch.
  • Change: ΔskewW = skewW − skewPRE2H, the same shock against its own two hours before the build. Measure of record: ΔskewM5; companion ΔskewHELD.
  • Exit size share: exit resting HYPE / (exit + absorption resting HYPE), per-minute means; Δ = window minus PRE2H. Exit submit share (older measure, ACC): exit-side orders placed over all orders placed.
  • Worked example (shock p0005, MM01, 2025-04-28, position rose): in PRE2H the ask sat 2.86 bps and the bid 5.74 bps behind the touch, skew = 2.86 − 5.74 = −2.88 bps. In M5 the ask sat 2.35 bps and the bid 3.54 bps behind, skew = −1.19 bps, so ΔskewM5 = +1.69 bps: this shock leaned less toward the exit than before the build.
How the quote state was built
  • One engine for all 812 shocks: order lifecycles from the raw HYPE order store (a limit order rests from placement to its cancel or fill, partial fills reduce it, orders with no terminal row dropped), resting state on a 1-minute grid, the engine behind the §4.4 order skews. Every placement day from the day before the earliest window to the last window day is read, so the order-day gap of the population build cannot occur.
  • The 468 shocks near an event window get the same shock-centred windows as the 344 outside; the event windows of §11.4 are rebuilt separately only to validate the engine.
  • The size-weighted distance is computed only over minutes with a known touch, so the zero-distance defect of the Exp9 minute files (a stored 0 where the touch is missing) cannot enter.
  • Code Exp9/code/pop812_quote_build.py (build, 317 dates, 14 minutes on 16 CPU), pop812_within_mm.py (tests, validation), pop812_fragment.py (this section). Built 2026-09-17.

Column key and source
Quantiles p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over shocks, one per line, then the number of shocks with the measure and the share of them leaning toward the exit (skew change below 0, share change above 0, submit share above 0.5). Classes under the 10 / 60 cuts. Δbest-quote skew: (exit-side best-quote distance to the touch minus absorption-side distance) in the window minus the same in PRE2H, bps of mid; negative = the exit quote moved nearer the touch than the absorption quote. A shock has the value only when both sides quote in both windows. Δexit size share: exit-side resting HYPE over both sides, window minus PRE2H. Exit submit share: exit-side share of orders placed in ACC. Windows: M5 = first 5 minutes after the own peak; HELD = own peak to own peak + min(T60, 120) min; UNW = own peak to + 2 h; ACC = build start to own peak; PRE2H = 2 h before the build start. The same table under 30 / 120 and for two-sided quoters is in the source. Every date included. Source Exp9/tables/pop812_tilt_by_class.csv; per shock pop812_quote_rows.csv.
  • The first-5-minute lean is common and does not rise with speed.
    Median ΔskewM5 is −4.1 bps for fast, −5.8 for medium and −3.4 for slow shocks. It comes from the absorption quote stepping back (median +2.9 bps against PRE2H) more than from the exit quote stepping in (−0.6 bps), as in §4.4.
  • The size lean does rise with speed.
    Median Δexit size share over M5 is +0.21 / +0.14 / +0.04 for fast / medium / slow. The next table shows this gradient sits between MMs.
  • Over two hours the order flips.
    Median ΔskewUNW is −0.1 bps for fast and −1.9 for slow shocks: a slow shock is still on the book and still leaning, a fast one is done.

  • Between MMs the size and submit shares still order speed.

  • The two-hour change is the one within-MM relation, and it runs the other way.
    Within MM ρ = −0.28: a shock that is still leaning over two hours is one that has not recovered. This is the state effect of §12.3 (the lean lasts while the position is held), not a lean that speeds the unwind.

  • The engine reproduces the published event-window values.
    On the 247 sample (a) rows whose stored table has order state (294 rows still join), median |difference| is 0.00 in every stored skew, size and submit column, and 97% to 100% of rows sit inside tolerance. 47 of the 298 stored rows carry zero order state from the order-day gap of the population build.
  • The 468 reproduce the sample (a) statistics of §11.4.
    Recomputed from the stored values the 18 published ρ match to 1e-4; from the rebuilt quote state they move by a median 0.027 (max 0.08), with 16 of 18 keeping their sign.
  • Touch distances match the Exp9 minute files.
    On 156 shared rows the exit best-quote distance over UNW matches to 0.00 bps at the median.
What this does not establish
  • Causation in either direction. A quote nearer the touch gets filled first, and being filled is the unwind.
  • The lean of record needs a quote on both sides in PRE2H and in M5: 565 of 812 shocks on 61 MMs have it. 231 shocks have no absorption-side order in M5 and 106 none on the exit side.
  • T60 runs on the 5-minute position grid from the peak bin while the windows start at the 1-minute own peak; under 10 / 60 the fast class is T60 of 5 or 10 minutes, so M5 overlaps most of a fast unwind.
  • The v3 catalogue (1,151 shocks) is not built. The roster’s frozen 181 are not used here.
  • Four published sample (a) rows no longer join the event × MM table, whose wallet codes were re-mapped on 2026-09-16; 13 other rows now join. This affects only the validation units, not the 812.

12. Quoting during the unwind

Event set 1: 7,492 shocked wallet-events inside 856 of the 915 net-flow boxes, every date included, 2025-10-10 among them, under the fill-based gate of the population build before the order-day fix (§4.1’s post-only rule gives 7,193 shocked wallet-events). t0 is the box start, the own peak is the wallet's largest excursion inside the box, and UNW is the two hours after it.
Terms used here: Event window, Shocked, Absorption side, exit side, ACC, UNW, Touch
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • ACC, UNW: ACC (accumulation) runs from t0 to the MM's own inventory peak; UNW (unwind) is the 2 hours after that peak. Each MM has its own boundaries.
  • Touch: the market's best price on that side: the best bid for a bid, the best ask for an ask.

In the 5 minutes after its own inventory peak, the median fast unwinder moves its exit-side quote 2.99 bps nearer the touch relative to its absorption-side quote, compared with its own two hours before the event, and 75% of fast rows move that way. The median slow unwinder moves it 0.79 bps the other way. This 5-minute change is the tilt measure of record, measured on the population of record in §12.5: the 35,612 event × MM rows that accumulated inventory. Over the two hours after the peak the fast change is 0.00 bps, so a two-hour average hides the lean. Sections 12.2 to 12.4 are older Exp9 tests, kept for the record. They use 7,492 shocked wallet-events on every date, 2025-10-10 included, two-hour and share-held windows, and recovery classes cut at 30 and 120 minutes to half.

Population and grain
  • Population. Every shocked wallet-event (|zdq| ≥ 3) of the population event study in an event window: 7,492 rows on 642 wallets, 856 events, 340 dates. The quantiles and tests use every row, 2025-10-10 included.
  • Grain. Resting orders per minute and side, rebuilt from the raw order store with the population study's lifecycle rule (an order rests from placement to its cancel or fill, partial fills reduce it, right-censored orders dropped). 4.14 million minute rows; 120 unwind-window minutes per wallet-event.

12.1 Definitions

Terms used here: Shocked, Minutes to half, Censored
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours). It is measured from the event end t1 on the position change over the event, so it is not the §4.4 unwind length T60, which runs from the MM’s own peak until 60% of the peak inventory is given back.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
Sides, windows, tilt and recovery class
  • Exit and accumulating sides. The exit side is the side whose fills reduce the position built in the event: the ask for a wallet whose position rose over the event, the bid otherwise. The accumulating side built it. This is SAME and OPP relabelled to the wallet's own position.
  • Windows. PRE2H = [t0 − 2 h, t0); ACC = [t0, own peak); UNW = [own peak, own peak + 2 h), with t0 the event start and the own peak the minute of the wallet's largest excursion inside the event.
  • Share still held. Each UNW minute is grouped by the wallet's excursion as a share of its peak excursion: 100–75%, 75–50%, 50–25%, 25–0%.
  • Distance to the touch. The wallet's best quote on a side against the market's best same-side price at that minute (last book state at or before; median staleness 0.1 s), in bps of mid; 0 is at the touch, positive behind it.
  • Exit-side shares. Exit-side share of resting size = mean exit-side resting HYPE over the mean of both sides, minutes without an order counting as zero. Exit-side share of submits is the same on order submits.
  • Tilt. tilt=dacc−dexit with each d the median over the window's minutes of the best quote's distance to the touch. Positive means the exit quote is closer to the touch. The size-weighted version uses the size-weighted mean distance of all resting orders.
  • Recovery class from minutes to half (after the event end, 1-minute grid, censored at 360): fast ≤ 30 minutes, medium 30 to 120, slow above 120 or censored.

  • On the two-hour window, every measure orders speed across MMs and barely within one.
    Across MMs |ρ| is 0.17 to 0.50; within a wallet it is under 0.12. The exit-side submit-share test on population shocks gave the same split (−0.48 across, −0.09 within).

    On the 4,109 rows with both sides present in at least half the unwind minutes, the size share is 0.50 in every class (pooled ρ = −0.03). The exit best quote sits 5.2, 6.4 and 11.1 bps from the touch for fast, medium and slow (pooled ρ = +0.36).
