    The exit quote's distance to the minute's best same-side maker fill price has pooled ρ = +0.24 and across-MM ρ = +0.51.
Limits
  • Whether the tilt causes the fast unwind. A wallet with 60% of its size on the exit side is filled there more often by construction, and a hedge on another venue or coin would produce the same HYPE path with no lean.
  • 68% of slow rows are censored at 360 minutes, so their ordering against uncensored slow rows carries no information.
  • The touch is the last book state at or before the minute; a quote posted inside the spread in that minute shows a negative distance, and the wallet's own order can be the touch.
  • 20 of 4.14 million minute rows lack a book state. Book staleness is 0.1 s at p50, 2.0 s at p95 and 3.9 s at p99.
  • Touch distances use the ts_bbo mid at the minute instant and mid-based columns the median trade mid of the minute; only the mid-based family is checked against the population table.
  • Every quantile and test here includes 2025-10-10. On 57 minute rows with resting orders and no market touch, the stored size-weighted distance to the touch is 0.0; it is treated as missing.

12.5 Fast unwinders lean toward the exit in the first 5 minutes; slow ones do not

  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Covered row: a row for which at least half of the orders behind the MM's pre-event post-only fills are found in the order store.
  • T60: minutes after the MM's own inventory peak until 60% of the accumulation is given back, on the 1-minute position rebuilt from fills.
Terms used here: Event window, HYPE MM, Active MM, sig24, Shocked, Absorption side, exit side, PRE2H, PRE30, POST, Markout M30, M60, M120, Taker share, ALO, IOC, GTC, Submits, cancels, Covered row, Episode, Touch, T60, One-sided, two-sided, rho, Quantile cells, A, L, t*
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • HYPE MM: a wallet the project's daily label model (v5d) classes as a HYPE market maker on that date. The label is per date.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • Markout M30, M60, M120: what a fill is worth against the mid 30, 60 or 120 minutes later, in bps of the fill's USD; positive is favourable to the wallet.
  • Taker share: the share of a wallet's fill USD in which its own order crossed the spread.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Submits, cancels: new limit orders and cancels. The venue records a modify as one cancel plus one new order, so cancels per submit sits near 1.
  • Covered row: a row for which at least half of the orders behind the MM's pre-event post-only fills are found in the order store.
  • Episode: a group of roster shocks that overlap in time.
  • Touch: the market's best price on that side: the best bid for a bid, the best ask for an ask.
  • T60: minutes after the MM's own inventory peak until 60% of the accumulation is given back, on the 1-minute position rebuilt from fills. It is not the T60 of §11.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the hit side's taker USD surges and the other side's does not; two-sided when both surge.
  • rho: Spearman rank correlation, from −1 to +1; p tests rho = 0.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.
  • A, L, t*: A is the most HYPE the MM built on the absorption side inside the window, counted from its position at t0; t* is the first minute attaining it. L is how far the position at t* sits from the MM's median position over the 6 hours before t0. Both are compared with the same sig24.
Event set 1, population of record: the 35,612 event × MM rows that accumulated inventory, on all 914 net-flow boxes, 2025-10-10 included. The 6,236 shocked accumulators, on 820 events, are reported beside them. Every window after the peak starts at t*, the MM’s own inventory peak, so two MMs in the same event have different clocks.

In the 5 minutes after its own inventory peak, the median fast unwinder moves its exit-side quote 2.99 bps nearer the touch relative to its absorption-side quote, compared with the same MM’s two hours before the event, and 75% of fast rows move that way. The median slow unwinder moves it 0.79 bps the other way. Among the 6,236 shocked accumulators the fast change is 4.33 bps toward the exit and the slow change 0.45 bps. While the MM still holds more than 40% of its accumulation, the companion window, the fast change is 4.41 bps against 0.56 bps for slow. Over the two hours after the peak the fast change is 0.00 bps: the lean lasts minutes, and the two-hour average is background. At the median nobody crosses the spread to get out. Speed comes from volume on both sides. In the two hours after the peak a fast MM fills 7.98 times its accumulation on the exit side and 6.61 times on the absorption side, and the position leaves as the difference. A slow MM fills 0.50 and 0.67 times.

What changed from the 2026-09-16 version.
  • Population. The earlier version used the 25,705 rows of the own-sigma rule. This version uses the 35,612 rows that pass the own-sigma rule or the population rule among active MMs, and reports the shocked MMs separately.
  • “Fast MMs do not tilt at all”
    holds only for the two-hour average. Over the minutes they still hold the position, fast MMs lean the most (Table 79).
  • “Inside an MM, more tilt goes with a slower unwind”
    also came from the two-hour window. Over the first 5 minutes after the peak, faster MMs lean more, mostly between MMs (ρ −0.53 across MMs, −0.04 inside an MM) (Table 82).
  • Unchanged. The exit-side taker share is 0 at the median in every class. Exit-side fills after the peak lose money for the fast and middle classes.
  • Dropped here. The early and late labels of §4.4. Early is almost entirely the fast class measured against the price clock, and the decision on that label is open.

Who is in the test

  • Active MM. A HYPE MM on the event date with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the two hours before the box starts (§4.1). 120,142 event × MM rows, 914 events, 2,132 MMs.
  • Accumulation A. On the MM’s 1-minute position path qt, rebuilt from its own fills, xt = s (qt − qt0) is the inventory built since the box start t0, with s = +1 when takers sell and −1 when they buy. A is the largest xt inside the box and t* is the first minute that reaches it.
  • Own rule. A is at least one of the MM’s own sigma (sig24), its position at t* is at least one sig24 away from its median position over the six hours before the box starts, and its absorption-side maker fills exceed its opposite-side fills. For an MM with sig24 = 663 HYPE, the median in this population, it must build 663 HYPE. 25,081 rows.
  • Population rule. A is at or above the 75th percentile of A across the event’s active MMs, and its absorption-side maker fills exceed its opposite-side fills. The threshold is 604 HYPE at the median event (392 at p25, 989 at p75). This rule adds large MMs whose accumulation is normal for them. 28,530 rows.
  • Accumulators. Rows that pass either rule: 35,612 rows, 914 events, 890 MMs. Shocked accumulators also clear the shock rule of §4.1 (a position change over the box of at least 3 times the MM’s own position scale): 6,236 rows, 820 events, 568 MMs.

Speed classes, windows and equations
  • T60. Minutes after t* until xt first falls to 0.4 A (60% given back), on the 1-minute grid, capped at 360. Fast: T60 ≤ 10. Middle: 11 to 60. Slow: above 60 or never within 6 hours. The median T60 is 4 minutes for fast rows, 26 for middle and 360 (the cap) for slow. Fixed cuts rather than terciles, because a quarter of all rows never reach 60% within 6 hours (§12.3 uses the Exp9 cuts of 30 and 120 minutes on a different population).
  • Windows. All windows after the peak start at t*, the MM’s own peak minute, not at a point of the event:
    PRE2H = [t0 − 2 h, t0), the baseline, two hours before the box starts;
    UNW = [t*, t* + 2 h), two hours after the peak;
    H60 = [t*, t* + min(T60, 120) min), while the MM still holds more than 40% of A: a median 4 minutes for fast rows, 26 for middle, 120 for slow;
    first 5 min = [t*, t* + 5 min) and first 15 min = [t*, t* + 15 min), fixed clocks of the same length for every class.
  • Distances. Every minute the MM’s resting post-only and GTC orders are read at the minute instant. dside is the median over the window’s minutes of the closest order’s distance to that side’s best price, in bps of mid, 0 at the touch, positive behind it.
  • Skew. skew = dabsorption − dexit, so a positive skew means the exit-side quote is nearer the touch. The change is Δskew = skewwindow − skewPRE2H on the same row: a positive Δskew means the exit-side quote moved nearer the touch relative to the absorption-side quote, that is, toward the exit, and “toward exit” is the share of rows with Δskew > 0. Every signed skew number in this section, in tables and text, reads this way. Section 11.5 writes the skew the other way round, dexit − dabsorption, so the same lean is negative there: +2.99 bps here reads −2.99 bps there.
  • Throughput. Exit fills / A = (exit-side maker + taker HYPE in UNW) / A; refills / A = absorption-side HYPE in UNW / A; net / A = the difference.
  • Markouts. mh = s (mid(t + h) − p) n for a fill of size n at price p, sign s = +1 for a buy; bps = 10,000 × Σmh / Σvolume over the class’s maker fills in the window and on the side (§4.1).

Column key and source

Volume-weighted markouts of maker fills in the window on the side; positive is money made by the MM. The 5- and 60-minute horizons are in the source table. The shocked fast class has $0.12bn of maker volume while held, so its cells are noisy. Source tables/unwind0917_markouts.csv.

  • In the first 5 minutes after the peak, the measure of record, fast unwinders lean toward the exit and slow unwinders lean away.
    The fast class moves its skew 2.99 bps toward the exit (75% of rows), the middle class 2.41 bps (68%), and the slow class 0.79 bps away from it (45% toward). Among shocked accumulators the fast class moves 4.33 bps (79%), the middle class 3.62 bps (77%) and the slow class 0.45 bps (53%), all toward the exit. The 5-minute window is the same clock for every class.
  • While the MM still holds more than 40% of its accumulation, the companion window, fast unwinders lean more.
    The fast class moves its skew 4.41 bps toward the exit (80% of rows) and the slow class 0.56 bps (57%). Among shocked accumulators it is 5.39 against 1.13 bps. This window lasts a median 4 minutes on fast rows and 120 on slow rows, so it compares different lengths.
  • In the first 5 minutes the lean follows the side the MM’s own fills are on, in every speed class.
    Rows whose exit-side fills exceed their absorption-side fills in those minutes move the skew toward the exit by 3.05 bps (fast), 3.03 bps (middle) and 1.78 bps (slow). Slow rows that still fill more on the absorption side move it 3.02 bps away. 8,957 of the 9,340 fast rows fill more on the exit side, against 4,195 of the 17,594 slow rows, so the class medians differ mostly by this mix (Table 89).
  • Averaged over two hours, the background window, the fast lean disappears.
    Over the two hours after the peak the fast class moves its skew 0.00 bps and the slow class 0.55 bps toward the exit. A lean of a few minutes averaged with the rest of the two hours is zero at the median. §12.3 found the same dependence on the share still held, on the older Exp9 shocks.
  • The lean is mostly the absorption-side quote stepping back.
    While held, the fast class moves its absorption-side quote +2.84 bps away and its exit-side quote −0.73 bps nearer; the exit side’s share of resting size rises by +0.059.
  • No class takes liquidity to get out.
    The exit-side taker share changes by 0 at the median in every class and window, and exit-side taker fills are 0.00 of A at the median for fast accumulators (0.06 for shocked ones).
  • Fast MMs get out by trading more on both sides, not by trading one side.
    On the exit side fast MMs fill 7.98, slow MMs 0.50 times A; on the absorption side fast MMs fill 6.61, slow MMs 0.67. Fast MMs place a median 39 exit-side orders per minute after the peak and cancel almost all of them; slow MMs place 7.5.
  • The ordering runs mostly between MMs.
    On the first 5 minutes the rank correlation of T60 with the lean is −0.53 across MMs and −0.04 inside an MM. Inside an MM the effect is weak but not absent: among the 115 MMs with at least three fast and three slow rows, the fast rows lean more in 68% of them, by a median +1.24 bps. Among shocked accumulators only 27 MMs qualify and the share is 48%.
  • Over two hours, getting out costs the fast and middle classes.
    Against the mid 30 minutes later, their exit-side maker fills over the two hours are worth 9.5 bps (fast) and 13.5 bps (middle) less than the fill price. Their absorption-side fills after the peak are worth 13.8 and 19.8 bps more. In bps, the slow class’s exit fills make +7.2. Maker and taker markouts over the first 5 and 15 minutes and the held window, against their pre-event values, are in §12.6.
Remarks that need attention
  • Slow rows with no fill on either side in the first 5 minutes still move their skew 2.42 bps away from the exit, because their exit-side quote moves 2.74 bps away from the touch (Table 89). The unwind does not explain a move without fills. Test: for these rows, split the exit-quote change into the touch moving (same order price, new best price) and the MM repricing (the best exit order cancelled and replaced farther out), from the order lifecycles.
  • Shocked slow accumulators move their skew 0.45 bps toward the exit in the first 5 minutes, while all slow accumulators move it 0.79 bps away. Shocked slow rows fill more on the exit side more often; reweighted to the fill-side mix of all slow rows, their median is 0.03 bps toward the exit, so the mix explains most of the gap but not its sign (Table 89). Test: repeat the fill-side split without 2025-10-10 and without the five MMs with the most shocked slow rows, and check whether the shocked exiting rows still lean more than all exiting slow rows (2.99 against 1.78 bps).

What this does not establish: the speed classes are defined on the outcome, so a class comparison is not the effect of a strategy chosen before the event, and a large two-sided flow shortens T60 mechanically for a given A. Quotes are read at the minute instant, while the median order in the ten inspected episodes lives 0.7 to 5.7 seconds, so distances describe the part of the book that survives a minute boundary. These rows read orders from every placement day from the day before the box, so the order-day gap fixed in §4.1 does not reach them: median absorption-side quote presence in the two hours before the event is 0.94 both on the 27% of rows that gap had flagged and on the rest. Order-message rates exist only for rows with A ≥ 0.5 sig24.

Earlier version (2026-09-16)

Superseded on 2026-09-17 by the version above. Its numbers are correct for the two-hour window on its population; the readings “fast and early MMs do not tilt at all” and “inside an MM, more tilt goes with a slower unwind” do not survive the windows that start at the peak.

On the 25,705 own-rule accumulators of §4.4, the fast and early MMs do not tilt their quotes at all while they unwind; the slow and late MMs tilt by about one basis point, by moving the absorption-side quote away rather than by bringing the exit-side quote in. No class crosses the spread to get out: the exit-side taker share is zero at the median before and during the unwind. The exit-side fills of every class but the slowest lose money over the next 30 to 120 minutes, and the absorption-side fills that continue after the peak make it.

Setup, definitions and equations
  • Rows. The 25,705 event × MM rows of §4.4 (accumulation A ≥ 1 sig24, level L ≥ 1 sig24, absorption-side maker fills above opposite-side fills), on all 914 events including 2025-10-10; the version without 2025-10-10 (25,561 rows) is in the source tables and moves the class medians of Table 87 by at most 0.21 bps.
  • Windows. PRE2H = [t0 − 2 h, t0); ACC = [t0, t*); UNW = [t*, t* + 2 h), where t* is the wallet's own absorption-side peak (§4.4).
  • Sides. SAME is the absorption side, OPP the exit side. Skew = SAME distance − OPP distance, so a positive skew means the exit-side order is nearer the touch.
  • Speed classes (T60). T60 is the number of minutes after t* until 60% of A is given back, on the 1-minute position grid, capped at 360 (never within 6 h). Fast: T60 ≤ 10 min (7,014 rows, 27%). Middle: 11 to 60 min (6,120, 24%). Slow: above 60 min or never (12,571, 49%; 26% of all rows never reach 60% within 6 h). Fixed cuts, not quantiles: T60 has no natural break and a quarter of rows are censored, so a tercile cut would fall at 197 minutes inside the censored mass. The 5 / 120 cuts are the sensitivity, in the source tables.
  • Timing classes. The §4.4 labels: early (half of A given back by the price extreme, the most extreme mid from the box start to half an hour after its end, 5,340), late holding more than half (16,510), late with the peak after the price extreme (3,855).
  • Quotes. 1-minute snapshots of the wallet's resting post-only and GTC limit orders. The touch is the market's best same-side level as of the minute. Best-level distance = median over the window's minutes with an order of the closest order's distance to the touch, in bps of mid, 0 at the touch. Size-weighted distance = resting-size-weighted mean distance over all order-minutes. Size = mean resting HYPE per minute, 0 in minutes with no order. The change is UNW − PRE2H for the same row; "toward exit" is the share of rows whose change has the sign that tilts toward getting out.
  • Markouts. For a fill of size n at price p with sign s (+1 buy, −1 sell), mh = s (mid(t + h) − p) n, from the stored columns of the grouped trade table, verified against a rebuild from the book within 0.03 bps on ordinary days and 0.41 bps on 2025-10-10. The table shows 10,000 × Σmh / Σvolume over all fills of the class in the window and on the side, maker and taker together.
  • Source. tables/unwind0915_skewmk_class_counts.csv, _quotes.csv, _markouts.csv, _within_mm.csv; 16 of 19 validation checks pass (row count, key uniqueness, 120 minutes per window, book staleness, mid-distance medians against the §4 population columns, fill USD against the §4.4 build).

Column key and source

Every fill of the class's wallets in the window (maker and taker together), on the absorption side and on the exit side; volume is the summed fill USD. Source tables/unwind0915_skewmk_markouts.csv, sample "every date", role "all".

  • The classes differ in book shape before the event, not in tilt.
    Fast and early MMs quote both sides about 4.1 bps from the touch with 372 HYPE resting on the exit side; slow MMs sit 9.8 bps away with 47 HYPE. The median skew is zero in every class before the event.
  • Slow and late MMs tilt about one basis point toward the exit during the unwind; fast and early MMs do not tilt at all.
    The median paired change in the best-level skew is +1.14 bps for the slow class and +0.80 for late holders, against +0.00 for the fast class and +0.00 for early unwinders. The tilt comes from the absorption side moving away (+0.55 bps, slow), not from the exit side coming in (-0.24 bps).
  • Nobody crosses to get out.
    The exit-side taker share of the wallet's own volume is 0 at the median in every class, before and during the unwind; the paired change is 0.
  • Inside an MM, more tilt goes with a slower unwind.
    Among the 96 MMs with at least three fast and three slow rows, the own fast-unwind skew change minus the own slow-unwind skew change has a median of -0.77 bps, and the fast rows show the larger tilt in only 35% of them. Across MMs the rank correlation of T60 with the skew change is -0.13, pooled +0.08. This is the §12.4 result on a population three times larger: the exit lean does not buy speed.
  • The exit fills lose and the continued absorption fills gain.
    In the unwind window, exit-side fills mark out at -10.9 bps (fast) and -13.5 bps (late holders) at 30 minutes, while absorption-side fills made after the peak mark out at +11.1 and +18.3 bps. The price keeps moving in the surge direction after the wallet's own peak, so getting out costs and staying in pays over the next two hours. Only the slow class's exit fills come out ahead (+4.9 bps at 30 minutes, -3.5 at 120): they exit late enough that the move has run.
  • The accumulation itself is the expensive part.
    Absorption-side fills inside ACC mark out at -71.0 bps (early) to -53.5 bps (late holders) at 30 minutes; the exit-side fills made during the same window mark out at +92.3 and +78.4. Early unwinders take the largest hit per dollar absorbed and give the position back within minutes.

What this does not establish: the classes are defined on the outcome (T60, or the give-back at the price extreme), so a within-class markout is not the return to a strategy chosen before the event. The quote rows exist only for the 74% of rows on order-covered dates (§4.1). Sensitivity at the 5 / 120 cuts and with the 1-minute T60 rows dropped is in the source tables.

12.6 Taker orders, cancels and markouts after the peak

Right after its inventory peak a fast unwinder sends more exit-side flow as taker orders and cancels more on the exit side, while most fast rows still send no taker order at all. In the first 5 minutes the fast class’s exit-side taker USD per minute is 6.82 times its rate in the two hours before the event, and taker orders carry 0.198 of its exit-side USD against 0.138 before. The rate rises on 28% of fast rows. Exit-side cancels rise from 64.9 to 102.4 per minute; absorption-side cancels stay at 66.0. The cancelled exit-side orders sit nearer the touch than before the event and the cancelled absorption-side orders farther away, the same direction as the quote lean of §12.5. Population: the 35,612 accumulators of record, every date; the shocked subset is in the toggles.

Symbols used in this section
  • Accumulator: an event × MM row that passes the own rule (A ≥ 1 sig24, the peak level at least 1 sig24 from its six-hour median, absorption-side maker fills above opposite-side fills) or the population rule (A at or above the 75th percentile of A over the event’s active MMs, same fill condition). 35,612 rows on 914 events, the population of record. Shocked accumulators also have |z| ≥ 3 on the position change over the 30-minute net-flow box: 6,236 rows.
  • A: the largest inventory the MM builds in the absorbing direction since the box start t0, in HYPE, on its 1-minute position path rebuilt from its own fills. sig24: the MM’s own scale for position swings over the 24 hours before t0, in HYPE.
  • t*: the first minute at which the inventory reaches A, the MM’s own peak. Every window after the peak starts there, so two MMs in one event have different clocks.
  • T60: minutes after t* until 60% of A is given back, capped at 360. Fast: T60 ≤ 10. Middle: 11 to 60. Slow: above 60 or never within 6 hours.
  • Windows: PRE2H = [t0 − 2 h, t0), the baseline; ACC = [t0, t*), the accumulation; M5 = [t*, t* + 5 min); M15 = [t*, t* + 15 min); H60 = [t*, t* + min(T60, 120) min), while the MM still holds more than 40% of A; UNW = [t*, t* + 2 h).
  • Absorption side: the MM’s order side that the event’s takers fill (its bids when takers sell). Exit side: the other side; exit-side fills reduce the inventory.
  • Taker fill: a fill of the MM’s own order that crossed the spread. Taker order: a distinct order id among those fills. Maker fill: a fill of a resting order.
  • Markout Mh for a fill of size n at price p with sign s (+1 buy, −1 sell): s (mid(t + h) − p) n; bps = 10,000 × ΣMh / Σ fill USD over the cell. Positive is money made by the MM. M5, M30, M120: 5, 30 and 120 minutes.
  • Cancel: a resting limit order (IOC excluded) whose last status is a cancel. Distance to the touch of a cancelled order: limit price behind the same-side best price, in bps of the mid, both taken from the last book state strictly before the cancel; 0 at the touch, negative inside the spread. Resting distance: the resting-size-weighted distance to the touch of the MM’s orders at the minute instants of the same window.
  • bps: basis points.

Skew compares the distances of the MM’s closest exit-side and absorption-side orders to the same-side best price, read at minute instants; a change toward the exit means the exit-side quote moved nearer the touch relative to the absorption-side quote.   • Speed sets the mix.
    8,957 of 9,340 fast rows fill more on the exit side in those minutes, against 4,195 of 17,594 slow rows.

Column key and source

Each cell, one value per line: (1) cancels per minute, pooled (summed cancels over summed window minutes); (2) cancels per new order, pooled; (3) distance to the touch of the cancelled orders, weighted by the HYPE still resting at the cancel, pooled over all cancels of the class, bps; (4) the same distance per row, median over rows; (5) resting distance to the touch of the same rows’ orders in the same window, read at minute instants, median over rows with both; (6) share of those rows whose cancelled orders sat farther from the touch than their resting orders; (7) share of cancelled HYPE within 1 bps of the touch. Distance: limit price behind the same-side best price in bps of the mid, both from the last book state strictly before the cancel (ts_bookdiff_lt, ts_bbo); 0 at the touch. A cancel is a resting limit order whose last status is a cancel; IOC orders are excluded. Line 3 is dominated by a few large far orders; line 4 is the typical row. Windows: PRE2H (the two hours before the box start t0), ACC (accumulation, t0 to the own peak t*), M5 and M15 (the first 5 and 15 minutes after t*), H60 (from t* while more than 40% of the accumulation A is still held, at most 120 minutes), UNW (the two hours after t*). Every date. Source tables/review0917_unwind_cancels.csv (built from the order store for all 35,612 rows); distance quantiles in Table 94; the shocked subset, distances to the mid and per-row cancel-rate changes are in the source table.

Column key and source

Lines 1 to 5: p5, p25, p50, p75, p95 across rows of the row’s cancelled-HYPE-weighted distance to the touch, bps of mid, book state strictly before each cancel. After the dash, lines 7 to 11: the same quantiles of that distance minus the row’s resting-size-weighted distance in the same window, read at minute instants; positive means the cancelled orders sat farther from the touch. Windows: PRE2H (the two hours before the box start t0), ACC (accumulation, t0 to the own peak t*), M5 and M15 (the first 5 and 15 minutes after t*), H60 (from t* while more than 40% of the accumulation A is still held, at most 120 minutes), UNW (the two hours after t*). Every date. Source tables/review0917_unwind_cancels.csv, columns can_vw_touch_p*, can_minus_resting_touch_p*.

  • Nearly every order ends in a cancel, in every class and window. Cancels per new order are 0.93 to 0.98.
  • Fast unwinders cancel more on the exit side right after the peak.
    Exit-side cancels per minute go from 64.9 in PRE2H to 102.4 in M5 and 102.1 in H60; absorption-side cancels go from 65.1 to 66.0 and 56.1. Slow: exit side 20.3 to 24.5, absorption side 22.4 to 25.9.
  • Where fast unwinders cancel mirrors their quote lean.
    The row-median distance of cancelled exit-side orders goes from 8.9 bps in PRE2H to 7.8 in M5 and 7.2 in H60, and 10% of cancelled exit-side HYPE sits within 1 bps of the touch before against 12% and 13% after. On the absorption side the distance goes from 9.1 to 11.7 and 12.5 bps, and the share within 1 bps from 9% to 4% and 2%.

Column key and source

Each cell, one value per line: M5, M30 and M120 (markouts at 5, 30 and 120 minutes, volume-weighted bps, positive = money made by the MM), then the fill USD of the cell. Maker fills are fills of resting orders; taker fills crossed the spread. The PRE2H row (the two hours before t0) is the benchmark on the same side and role: before the event the absorption side already marks out negative and the exit side positive at 30 and 120 minutes, because those horizons run into the event. Windows: PRE2H (the two hours before the box start t0), ACC (accumulation, t0 to the own peak t*), M5 and M15 (the first 5 and 15 minutes after t*), H60 (from t* while more than 40% of the accumulation A is still held, at most 120 minutes), UNW (the two hours after t*). Markouts come from the stored columns of the grouped trade table, within 0.03 bps of a book rebuild on ordinary days and 0.41 bps on 2025-10-10. The two-hour (UNW) values are in the source table; maker M30 over H60 and UNW reproduces the page’s earlier markout table within 0.001 bps. Every date. Source tables/review0917_unwind_markouts.csv; the shocked subset is Table 96.

Column key and source

Lines as in Table 95: M5, M30, M120 (markouts at 5, 30, 120 minutes, volume-weighted bps) and fill USD. PRE2H is the two hours before t0; M5, M15 and H60 start at the own peak t*. The fast cells are thin and dominated by one date: 2025-10-10 carries 22% of the fast class’s exit-side maker USD in M5 and 27% on the absorption side, and without that date the M5-window maker M30 is −19.0 bps (exit) and +24.7 bps (absorption). Every date is kept in the table. Source tables/review0917_unwind_markouts.csv, columns oct10_volume_share, M30_bps_excl_20251010, top5_mm_share.

Remarks that need attention
  • In M5 the fast class’s exit-side maker fills mark out at −28.0 bps at 5 minutes, against +2.0 bps on the same side before the event, and its absorption-side maker fills at +43.6 against −1.4. Its exit-side taker fills in M5 mark out at +7.6 at 5 minutes and +48.3 at 30 minutes. The unwind speed does not explain these signs; the price path after the peak may. Test: per row, the mid change from t* to t* + 5, 30 and 120 minutes in the direction of the event’s taker flow, and the markouts recomputed net of it.
  • Among shocked fast accumulators, exit-side maker fills in M5 mark out at +131.7 bps at 30 minutes with every date and −19.0 without 2025-10-10, which carries 22% of that volume. Test: rebuild the 2025-10-10 markouts from ts_bbo with the date-safe rule of the stored-column audit and re-read the cell.
  • Cancelled orders sit nearer the touch than the orders resting at minute instants in every class and window, before the event too: fast exit side 8.9 against 12.1 bps in PRE2H, with the cancelled orders farther on 41% of rows. The ten inspected episodes of the analysis record found cancels selecting farther-placed orders. A minute snapshot misses orders that live a few seconds near the touch, so the gap may be sampling. Test: compare cancelled orders with all orders placed in the same window, by placement distance weighted by size, instead of with minute snapshots.
  • Slow accumulators raise their absorption-side taker USD rate during the accumulation (2.32 times PRE2H) and in the first 5 minutes after the peak (1.70 times), crossing the spread in the direction that adds to the position. Test: split those taker fills by minute relative to the price extreme and by MM, with the five largest MMs’ share of the cell.

What this does not establish: the speed classes are defined on the outcome, so a class comparison is not the effect of a strategy chosen before the event. Rates pooled over rows are carried by the most active MMs; the per-row medians of the taker changes are zero. Cancel distances use the book state strictly before each cancel; resting distances use minute instants, so the two are read on different clocks. About 27% of rows fall on dates with holes in the order store, which lowers cancel and submit counts there.
